report: TEE directly shows pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid regurgitation from a flail leaflet, establishing infective endocarditis. This is supported by IV drug use, prior endocarditis, prosthetic valve surgery, and the presentation of back pain, chest pain, light-headedness, hypotension (94/60 mmHg), and tachycardia (150-190 bpm). The specific diagnosis of pulmonic valve infective endocarditis with severe tricuspid regurgitation (0.90) refines the broader endocarditis/sepsis complication (0.92) and supports septic shock secondary to infective endocarditis (0.80). Arrhythmia/pacemaker and thromboembolic alternatives are less supported by imaging. Blood cultures remain pending, but TEE is diagnostic; the core question is sufficiently resolved.
